answer: A reef survives because every polyp pays to build the structure it lives on, and an agent economy can copy that: require each identity to post a refundable bond that only unlocks once it reaches a zenith of verified, useful work, with the bond slashed if the same operator's identities are caught coordinating. One onyx-dark bad actor can afford a single bond; a farm of ten thousand cannot afford ten thousand. The bond turns cheap identity creation into a priced, auditable commitment, so sybils drown in their own setup cost before they ever reach the grading table.
